## Liberty Hospital continues to achieve growth milestones

August 2026

Liberty Hospital continues to grow services and sites of care as part of The University of Kansas Health System. Below are some of our recent activities:

  * A new vascular surgery clinic opened at the end of July.
  * Planning is underway to open endocrinology services within a primary care setting this fall.
  * Urology and plastic surgery clinics also will open on the hospital campus this fall.
  * We are making building and infrastructure improvements to ensure we provide the safest care in the safest environment.
  * We are making progress toward our goal of bringing Epic (MyChart) to Liberty Hospital and clinics in the fall of 2027.

It is our mission to care for our community. It is our honor to continue expanding our services to provide exceptional care close to home for you.

Here, we grow! Be sure to follow our journey and check back for future updates.

June 25, 2026

The University of Kansas Infusion Therapy is now open at Liberty Hospital, providing more than 170 non-oncology medications, such as anti-inflammatory and steroid therapies; antibiotic, antifungal and antiviral therapies; biosimilars; catheter care; HIV therapies; hydration and electrolyte replacement; immunoglobins; monoclonal antibodies and more.

Services are conveniently located on the main floor of the hospital, near the main entrance. In addition to this critical care now being closer to home, plans are underway for several other new clinics and services to open in the coming months. Watch this page for announcements. Here, we grow!

April 1, 2026

Liberty Hospital joined The University of Kansas Health System to preserve and grow services, further enhance quality, and invest in our people and our community. We are doing all those things — and more! Here are some of our recent milestones:

· Eighteen new physicians across a variety of specialties are caring for patients at Liberty Hospital.

· Nephrology outpatient services opened in the Doctors Building, Suite 202, in January. Appointments may be scheduled by calling 816.415.3470.

· Neurology outpatient services opened in Suite 202 in March. To schedule an appointment, call 816.415.3472.

· Construction on The University of Kansas Cancer Center in Medical Plaza East is complete and houses medical oncology and radiation oncology. The space includes a new entry and waiting area, new pharmacy space, additional examination rooms and infusion bays. Work continues on the new laboratory.

· Nine exam rooms were added to the Liberty Clinic.

· All Liberty Hospital employees and Advanced Practice Providers are now officially employed by The University of Kansas Health System. Physicians are employed by The University of Kansas Physicians.

· We are making significant progress in aligning our technology infrastructure, with the goal of going live with Epic (MyChart) in the fall of 2027.

Liberty Hospital is a great place to give and receive care. We continue to look forward to even more opportunities to provide those in our community with exceptional care close to home.

Here, we grow! Be sure to follow our journey online – we look forward to updates with you!

## Growth continues at Liberty Hospital

January 30, 2026

Liberty Hospital joined The University of Kansas Health System to preserve and grow services, further enhance quality, and invest in our people and our community. We are doing all those things — and more! Here are some of our recent milestones:

  * Eighteen new physicians across a variety of other specialties are caring for patients at Liberty Hospital.
  * Nephrology outpatient services opened in the Doctors Building, Suite 202, on Jan. 15. Appointments may be scheduled by calling 816.415.3470.
  * Neurology outpatient services will open in Suite 202 beginning March 4. To schedule an appointment, call 816.415.3472.
  * Construction is completed on The University of Kansas Cancer Center on the ground floor of Medical Plaza East, which houses medical oncology and radiation oncology. The space includes a new entry and waiting area, new pharmacy space, additional examination rooms and infusion bays. Work continues on the new laboratory.
  * Nine exam rooms were added to The Liberty Clinic.
Together, we are fulfilling a promise to bring world-class healthcare to the Northland and northwest Missouri.

As you see changes during the next year — from new signage to new locations, physicians and providers available to you — we hope you’re as excited as we are.

Here, we grow! Be sure to follow our journey online – we look forward to sharing updates with you!

## Radiation oncology care now available in Liberty

September 22, 2025

To ensure patients living in and around the Northland have access to the cancer care they need closer to home, The University of Kansas Cancer Center in Liberty has launched radiation oncology services. Exams and simulations started on Sept. 8, and treatment services are set to start today. The facility features advanced technology, including a Siemens CT simulator and a Varian Truebeam linear accelerator. Radiation oncologist Julia Oh, MD, recently joined the cancer center and will work alongside Ajay Tejwani, MD, MPH, to provide patient care at the new location.

Here, we grow! Be sure to follow our journey online – we look forward to sharing updates with you!

As we continue into our second year, we look forward to even more opportunities to provide those in our community with exceptional care as well as the best quality, experience and results, close to home.

## The University of Kansas Cancer Center Now Open in Liberty

June 10, 2025

Today marks a milestone for patients living in and around the Northland as The University of Kansas Cancer Center opens its doors at Liberty Hospital. Patients will have access to medical oncology exams and infusion services this summer, with radiation oncology services launching this fall.
  * The University of Kansas Cancer Center medical oncologists started rounding on Liberty inpatients in January.
  * Nephrologists from the health system began rounding on inpatients in April and could see outpatients in a multispecialty clinic as early as this summer.
  * The University of Kansas Cancer Center will open medical oncology and radiation therapy services at Liberty Hospital this summer.

The goal of Liberty Hospital joining the health system is full integration, with access to expertise and resources across academic and community medicine. We are focused on what is best for patients, our people and the community.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Below are some of the questions we are most often asked by patients and community members. If you have a question, you may send it to us using the “Contact us” button to the right. Please include your contact information for a response.

What happens now?
Nothing changes for patients immediately. You can continue to see the same providers you know and trust in the same ways you currently do.

# VESHW is Building a New Hospital

#### Grand Opening

Image: VESHW new building sketch

We're proud to announce the construction of our new hospital on the west side of Wichita near 21st Street North and Hoover Road, across from Sedgwick County Zoo. We expect the nearby landmarks and reference points along with good visibility from the street will save pet owners time in an emergency situation. The eight month construction period of the 12,500-square-foot hospital will begin in October, and includes renovating and expanding an existing building. In addition to our emergency doctors, we have exceptionally qualified specialists in general surgery, radiology, oral surgery, and ophthalmology. Our future goal is to expand our specialties to include cardiology, dermatology, and oncology. The new hospital will be able to better accommodate our expansion of advanced diagnostics equipment, including our heart-echo, ultra-sound, and recently acquired CT scan, which is currently the only veterinary CT offered in Wichita. Advanced CT technology provides 3D views used to diagnose spinal injuries, fractures, brain tumors and masses that x-ray and ultra sound have limitations on. Our existing practice will remain in place as an urgent care and minor emergency facility in the evenings and on weekends. Critical care patients will be transferred from the current location to the new veterinary hospital. These renderings will give you a sneak peak at what's to come!

# Topping Out Ceremony Marks Major Progress on New Cancer Center Building

August 21, 2026

On August 21, 2026, The University of Kansas Cancer Center celebrated a key milestone in the construction of its new cancer research and clinical building with a ceremonial topping out. The steel beam, signed by faculty, staff, patients, construction partners and community supporters, was raised into place as a symbol of progress and shared commitment. Several dignitaries were in attendance, including U.S. Senator Jerry Moran.

The new building will bring together laboratories, clinical spaces and a Good Manufacturing Practice cellular therapy manufacturing area under one roof. For the first time in the cancer center’s history, researchers and patient care teams will work side by side. The work inside the building will focus on cellular therapy, a leading‑edge approach that uses a person’s own cells to more directly target their cancer. The building will also house the cellular therapeutics GMP laboratory, which will help expedite CAR T treatment for patients.

### The University of Kansas Cancer Center expands to 3 Northland locations

The University of Kansas Cancer Center is expanding the care it provides in the Northland by opening new locations at Briarcliff and Liberty Hospital. Ranked in the top 1% nationwide, the cancer center offers unrivaled expertise and experience in diagnosing and treating all forms of cancer, from common and complex to rare. This growth underscores the cancer center’s commitment to providing leading cancer care, access to clinical trials and the most advanced treatment options close to home.

The Briarcliff location will open in June 2025 and initially will provide medical oncology, as well as hematology exam and limited infusion services. This new location will be expanded in the fall to offer all oncology infusion services with an on-site pharmacy and laboratory services.

At the same time, a cancer center location will open at Liberty Hospital in summer 2025. Like the Briarcliff location, it will be a phased opening, initially offering medical oncology exam and infusion and adding radiation oncology in the fall.

With the addition of the Briarcliff and Liberty Hospital sites, the cancer center has 16 locations throughout Kansas and Missouri.
